answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to one secret yielding one nullifier per epoch; one claim keeps haven standing and earns the reward. A second action from the same secret conflicts, and the delta between the two transcripts lets anyone recover the secret — checkable proof of double-acting that slashes the reward. Each claim commits to the next epoch's vine of nullifiers, so a second claim forks one secret's vine and the fork is the evidence. One secret cannot cover two identities: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 secrets, while one honest agent keeps one secret and pays only a single claim.
